newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Gencor Nickel worth up to A$1.2 bln -report.
newsitem.headline: Gencor Nickel worth up to A$1.2 bln -report.

text.p: The independent report commissioned by QNI Ltd to assess its planned merger with Gencor Ltd's Billiton Nickel has valued Billiton Nickel's assets at between A$1.003 billion and A$1.209 billion, the report released on Tuesday showed.

The effective price to be paid by QNI for these assets was between A$1.094 billion and A$1.114 billion, given prices of A$2.40 a share to A$2.50 a share and the revised 455.802 million shares being issued to Billiton Nickel, the Grant Samuel and Associates report said.
"The value attributed to the QNI shares to be issued to Billiton falls within the estimated range of values for Billiton Nickel," the report said.
But the report said the acquisition would lead to a dilution in earnings per share and cashflow per share in the short term.
"In addition, a major part of QNI's assets will be located in Columbia involving both currency and country risks," it said.

Grant Samuel valued Billiton Nickel's major asset, the Cerro Matoso nickel mine in Colombia, at between US$691 million and US$816 million (A$933 million to A$1.103 billion), but it said other buyers might adopt a more conservative valuation.
